candidates.rationale: Denominator TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5)+eps is a 5-node block that must move. Swapping the time-series liquidity rank for a cross-sectional one leaves only SUB($close,$low) (3 nodes) shared with the parent, clearing the 4-node archive_subtree gate; nearby TS_RANK windows (e.g. 21) already failed correlation at rho 0.947 against this exact parent, so the axis itself (time-series vs cross-sectional) is the part that needed to change, not the window.

Numerator and denominator each independently exceed the 4-node archive_subtree cap (5 and 7 nodes) via the shared TS_MIN($low,21) term, so both occurrences must change together or one alone survives as an exact match. Replacing the floor anchor with a mean anchor turns the strict min-max Stochastic into a mean-reversion-style range position; window-only and single-anchor swaps on this parent already failed this round (rho 0.875-0.992, or archive_subtree on a window-only edit).

RANK and CS_RANK are literal aliases here, and smoothing the $close denominator already failed twice this round (duplicate at TS_MEAN w=5, rho 0.998 at w=21), so any monotonic change to price or to the outer rank cannot decorrelate. Taking the magnitude of EPS is the one available non-monotonic lever: it reorders loss-making names relative to the signed-yield ranking while leaving the majority (profitable) names' order untouched.

Raw $dollar_volume is a dominant archived level (TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) is its own archive member; light wrappers around raw/smoothed dollar_volume hit rho 0.968-0.997 this run), so the liquidity normalizer itself is the weak part. Swapping to the stock's own 21-day close volatility keeps the same close-low numerator but scales it by price dispersion instead of any volume transform, avoiding both the raw-volume trap and duplicating af43733e3a6a1dbf's TS_RANK(volume) fix.

The second leg is an 8-node block on its own, so swapping the other (2-node) fundamental leg instead would leave it byte-identical and fail archive_subtree regardless of which fundamental is chosen. Replacing the intraday-range numerator with a 3-day price change keeps the same eps-guarded close-scaling but trades range-positioning for short momentum; every same-family OHLC-anchor swap tried elsewhere this run (open/high/low substitutions) stayed at rho >= 0.85, so the core comparison needed to change, not just which anchor is used.

Confirms the round's own finding that fundamental-minus-volume-transform spreads beat fundamental-fundamental ones (RANK(eps)-RANK(TS_DELTA(dollar_volume,63)) is already archived at fitness 4.053). Both legs here were only 2 nodes each so a single-leg swap is structurally safe; using dispersion instead of the already-taken delta/level transforms avoids restating an existing archive member.

ADD(DELAY($close,1),eps) is a 5-node block that any leftover mutation keeps intact; a numerator field swap and an outer-window change on this exact parent both already failed archive_subtree this round. Replacing the single-day lag with a 5-day average converts the overnight-gap signal into an open-vs-recent-trend signal rather than another DELAY-lag variant, which is the untried axis for this shape.

CS_RANK(TS_DELTA(fundamental,63)) is flagged as a saturated 4-node block regardless of field, and it is exactly the second leg here. Swapping change-over-time for dispersion-over-time keeps the proven 63-day window (21-day fundamental diffs are mostly zero, 1-day fails coverage) while breaking the exact match with the archived parent in a single relabel, leaving the CS_RANK($accrual_gap) leg untouched since it is only 2 nodes.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.
